title: CLEAR-EO Newsletter No. 2
summary: As we close our first year, we look back at what we achieved and where the project is headed: our webinar series, CLEAR-EO at events around Europe, and the plans for year two.
body:
As we close our first year, we can start looking back at what we achieved, and foresee where the project is headed, now that it is running at full steam.

The project kickstarted last year with a meeting in Torino, and continued in February at EUMETSAT in Darmstadt, where we met alongside our sibling projects PANORAMA and GreenEO. In May we held the first meeting of our Advisory Board, and we thank its members for their valuable feedback.

Methodological work on our three applications (urban flash floods, agriculture, and air quality) was the core of the first year, while we are now slowly pivoting from methods to workflows. The Virtual Observatory, built around an enhanced Aviso notification system, is what will turn those methods into on-demand services triggered by events detected in the data. Meanwhile the data access platform is under development, the first test environments are deployed, and partners have supercomputing time on Leonardo, cloud resources on the European Weather Cloud, EOSC, and on-premise infrastuctures. Our webinar series, one of our most effective channels beyond the usual EO circles, will resume in Q4 2026.

Year two is where CLEAR-EO has to deliver end to end: components becoming a system, and that system meeting real requirements. We set that course starting tomorrow, when the consortium gathers in Vienna for our General Assembly. Thank you to everyone who got us this far.

**CLEAR-EO Webinar Series**

**World Meteorological Day Webinar**

**From Global Weather Observations to Local Earth Intelligence**

The webinar celebrated World Meteorological Day by demonstrating how global meteorological observations are transformed into practical decision support through Destination Earth and CLEAR-EO.

Starting with the role of the World Meteorological Organization and ECMWF, the webinar illustrated how new-generation meteorological satellite missions, AI and advanced forecasting systems are supporting three operational applications developed within CLEAR-EO:

* Urban flood resilience
* Climate-resilient agriculture
* Urban air quality

The session highlighted the complete information chain—from observations to Earth intelligence—and demonstrated how European investments are creating tangible societal benefits.

**Climate-Resilient Agriculture Webinar**

**From Sensors to Satellites**

Agriculture increasingly depends on timely climate information. This webinar showcased how CLEAR-EO combines:

* IoT observations from the gaiasense platform
* Copernicus Earth observation
* Meteorological forecasts
* Artificial intelligence

to deliver field-scale early warning services for drought, heavy rainfall and soil moisture anomalies.

Using the Thessaly pilot as an example, speakers discussed how farmers and agronomists are co-designing services following the devastating impacts of Storm Daniel. The webinar also connected local solutions to global agricultural monitoring through GEOGLAM and the Crop Monitor initiative.

**Drone-Enabled Flash Flood Intelligence**

Urban flooding is becoming more frequent and more destructive across Europe.

This webinar explored how drones can complement satellite observations and numerical weather prediction by providing rapid, high-resolution situational awareness during flood events.

Topics included:

* drone-based observations
* hydrological modelling
* real-time geospatial notifications
* OGC interoperability standards
* operational emergency management

The session demonstrated how CLEAR-EO integrates multiple observation sources into faster and more reliable flood decision support.

**Earth Observation for Cleaner Air**

Air quality remains one of Europe's major environmental challenges.

This webinar demonstrated how CLEAR-EO combines satellite observations, atmospheric modelling and ground-based measurements to improve urban air-quality monitoring and forecasting.

Using the Marseille application as an example, speakers showed how data from Copernicus, Destination Earth and advanced atmospheric models can support:

* local authorities
* environmental agencies
* public health organisations

with improved forecasting and decision support.

**Citizen Science and Digital Twins**

**Bringing Communities into Earth Intelligence**

Citizen observations are becoming an increasingly valuable component of Digital Twins of the Earth.

This webinar explored how citizen science complements satellite observations and in-situ monitoring while strengthening engagement between science, policy and society.

Presentations highlighted:

* citizen-generated environmental observations
* Digital Twins within Destination Earth
* interoperability and open standards
* community participation in environmental monitoring

The webinar demonstrated that Earth Intelligence becomes significantly more valuable when local communities actively contribute observations and knowledge.

**The CLEAR-EO Webinar Series**

Together, the webinars illustrate the complete CLEAR-EO vision:

**Earth observations → data integration → AI → Digital Twins → actionable Earth Intelligence**

Across all topics, several common themes emerge:

* integrating satellite, meteorological and in-situ observations;
* applying artificial intelligence to support decision making;
* exploiting Destination Earth and the European Weather Cloud;
* using interoperable data spaces and open standards to improve data sharing;
* engaging users through co-design and stakeholder participation;
* transforming scientific information into operational services for climate resilience.

Rather than presenting individual technologies, the webinar series demonstrates how these innovations work together to support resilient communities and informed environmental decision-making across Europe.

**CLEAR-EO Around Europe**

In addition to organising its own webinars, CLEAR-EO partners have actively contributed to major conferences, exhibitions and community events, helping to expand the project's impact.

**Agrotica 2026**

NEUROPUBLIC presented CLEAR-EO innovations for climate-smart agriculture during Agrotica 2026 in Thessaloniki.

The event provided an opportunity to showcase the project's agricultural services, including the integration of gaiasense IoT observations with satellite and climate information to support farmers with field-level early warnings.

**Destination Earth Community**

CLEAR-EO partners continue to contribute to the growing Destination Earth ecosystem through workshops, user exchanges and technical collaboration.

Project activities demonstrate how DestinE capabilities can be transformed into operational services by combining advanced modelling, Earth observation, AI and stakeholder co-design.

**European Big Data Value Forum (EBDVF)**

CLEAR-EO has contributed to discussions on data spaces, artificial intelligence and trusted data ecosystems, highlighting the importance of interoperable infrastructures for delivering operational Earth intelligence services.

**GEO and International Earth Observation Communities**

Several CLEAR-EO partners contribute actively to the Group on Earth Observations (GEO), Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC), Destination Earth and related international initiatives.

These contributions help ensure that CLEAR-EO developments align with international standards, promote interoperability and support wider uptake of Earth intelligence solutions beyond the project itself.

**XXV ISPRS Congress – Toronto, Canada**

CLEAR-EO partners Ithaca S.r.l. and Politecnico di Torino (SDG11Lab) presented the scientific contribution “Integrating Airborne LiDAR and OpenStreetMap Features for Automated Hydrological Conditioning of Urban Digital Elevation Models” at the XXV ISPRS Congress in Toronto, Canada.

Presented by Tommaso Destefanis, together with co-authors Elena Durando, Matilde Oliveti, Emanuele Artù Cassin and Martina Di Rita, the work showcases an automated open-source Python pipeline developed to integrate classified airborne LiDAR data with OpenStreetMap infrastructure features, including bridges, tunnels, culverts and flood defence barriers, to generate hydrologically conditioned digital elevation models for urban flood modelling.

Tested over a 16 km² area of central Copenhagen using 2023 national LiDAR data, the approach automatically modifies elevation data to represent key urban structures that influence surface water flow. The conditioning lowered 198,733 pixels at bridge, tunnel and culvert locations and raised 27,022 pixels along flood defence structures, reducing the volume of trapped depressions in the DSM by 5.0%. The resulting elevation model achieved a vertical accuracy of NMAD = 0.066 m when validated against the Danish national terrain model.

The conditioned DEM provides an important input to the CLEAR-EO urban flood simulation chain developed by the Danish Meteorological Institute, demonstrating how Earth Observation data, open geospatial information and automated processing can be combined to improve the representation of complex urban environments in flood modelling.

The paper has been published in the ISPRS Archives (Int. Arch. Photogramm. Remote Sens. Spatial Inf. Sci., XLIX-B2-2026, 151–159, DOI: 10.5194/isprs-archives-XLIX-B2-2026-151-2026).

Farmtopia Mou

Text from Farmtopia pubished July 2026

*“Farmtopia is pleased to announce the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with CLEAR-EO, a project that harnesses Earth Observation technologies to provide reliable environmental information for agriculture and natural resource management. CLEAR-EO’s expertise in satellite-based monitoring complements Farmtopia’s mission to democratise digital farming through accessible Agricultural Digital Solutions that support farmers’ everyday decision-making.*

*Under the Memorandum of Understanding, the two projects will work together on e.g. dissemination and communication activities, including joint press releases, communication campaigns, stakeholder engagement, participation in conferences, workshops and webinars, cross-promotion of project results, and the exchange of knowledge and experiences. The partnership will also explore opportunities to showcase how Earth Observation services and digital farming solutions can work together to support more sustainable agricultural practices.*

*Together,* *[Farmtopia](https://farmtopia.eu/)* *and* *[CLEAR-EO](https://clear-eo.eu/)* *aim to increase the adoption of data-driven solutions that help farmers manage their land more sustainably and efficiently.”*

**The 15th International Air Quality Conference**

CLEAR-EO partner **SUEZ** presented the scientific contribution **"Seamless Integration of Earth Observation Products, In-situ Data, and WRF/CHIMERE Modelling for Machine Learning Enhanced Air Quality Forecasts"** at the [15th International Conference on Air Quality](https://www.air-quality-conference.org/prague2026/) in Prague, Czech republic.

Presented by **Ines Makni** and colleagues, the work showcases the integrated forecasting framework being developed within the CLEAR-EO Urban Air Quality application. The approach combines multiple complementary data sources, including Copernicus Earth observation products, ground-based air quality measurements, and high-resolution atmospheric modelling using the WRF and CHIMERE models, to create more accurate and timely urban air quality forecasts.

A key innovation is the incorporation of machine learning techniques to improve forecast performance by learning from both model outputs and observational data. This seamless integration of satellite observations, in-situ monitoring and numerical modelling exemplifies the CLEAR-EO vision of transforming heterogeneous environmental data into actionable Earth Intelligence for public authorities, environmental agencies and citizens.

The presentation also demonstrated how interoperable data infrastructures and advanced analytics can strengthen operational air quality services, supporting better-informed decisions for public health and urban environmental management.

This item fits well within the newsletter because it demonstrates that CLEAR-EO is not only developing operational services but is also contributing new scientific advances to the international research community.

**NewSpace Africa Conference – Gabon**

As part of the CLEAR-EO project, SISTEMA participated in the NewSpace Africa Conference in Gabon, engaging with key stakeholders from across the African space and Earth Observation ecosystem. The event provided an excellent opportunity to present the objectives of CLEAR-EO, strengthen relationships with institutional and commercial partners, and explore how the project's capabilities can address regional needs. Discussions focused on emerging Earth Observation initiatives, climate services, and digital solutions, while also identifying new collaboration opportunities and potential future use cases within the African context.

**Destination Earth National Information Day – Barcelona, Spain**

Representing the CLEAR-EO project, SISTEMA attended the Destination Earth National Information Day in Spain to better understand the rapidly evolving DestinE ecosystem and its growing adoption across Spanish institutions and service providers. The event showcased a range of innovative applications leveraging DestinE data and services, providing valuable insights for the future integration of DestinE capabilities within CLEAR-EO. A highlight of the day was the visit to the national supercomputing facilities, offering a firsthand view of the high-performance computing infrastructure that enables Europe's Digital Twin Earth initiative.

**EO Commercialisation Forum – Seville**

SISTEMA participated in the EO Commercialisation Forum in Seville on behalf of the CLEAR-EO project, contributing to discussions on the future of the commercial Earth Observation sector. The event explored how emerging technologies, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructures, and evolving business models are transforming the EO market and creating new opportunities for downstream services. The knowledge gained will help position CLEAR-EO to maximise the impact and uptake of its services, ensuring that the project's solutions align with current market trends and the evolving needs of both public and private users.

**FAO Global Conference on Smart Farming – Rome**

As part of the CLEAR-EO project, SISTEMA participated in the [FAO Global Conference on Smart Farming](https://www.fao.org/events/detail/global-conference-on-smart-farming/en?utm_source=chatgpt.com), held at FAO Headquarters in Rome in early July 2026. The event brought together policymakers, researchers, industry representatives, and international organizations to discuss how Earth Observation, artificial intelligence, digital technologies, and data-driven services can accelerate the transition towards more sustainable and resilient agrifood systems. Participation allowed SISTEMA to engage with key stakeholders, strengthen links with the FAO community, and gather valuable insights to ensure that CLEAR-EO remains aligned with international priorities for climate-smart agriculture, operational crop monitoring, and digital decision-support services.

**Looking Ahead**

The CLEAR-EO webinar series will continue throughout the project, bringing together experts from research, public authorities, industry and international organisations.

Upcoming webinars will continue exploring the future of:

* Digital Twins
* Earth Intelligence
* Artificial Intelligence
* Data Spaces
* Operational climate services
* User-driven innovation

Together, these activities are building a growing European community that transforms Earth observation into practical solutions for society.

Date and time for the webinars fall 2026.
